- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction by 2–5% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) after a peak, model fails to adjust downward; force mean reversion toward recent 5–10 day average.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral or weak (0.00–0.33) and recent history shows downward trend; add 1–3% upward bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.00” values (strong bullish), model often fails to account for eventual correction; apply early warning lag correction (reduce forecast 1–2 days ahead of peak).
